executive_summary.headline: A phone agent, a pixel-art skill and a codebase mapper lead the week
executive_summary.body: wangzan101/Mika added 3,860 stars in three days by running Android apps on a hidden screen, patch-gg/pixelfx reached 2,597 with 244 pixel-art effects plus a skill to make more, and haydenschmitty/floorplan reached 1,790 by drawing a plain-English map of any app.

executive_summary.headline: Weights as programs is the week's fun find
executive_summary.body: A Show HN put an NES CPU inside Qwen3.5 weights (292 points), another ran MNIST through DOOM maps at 97.2%, and a third fit a language model in a boot sector.

executive_summary.headline: Creators get production pipelines
executive_summary.body: anymove turns one AI video into a rigged 3D move for about $3 by the maker's count, Frametell turns a sentence into a storyboarded explainer video, and Hallmark added 11,566 stars teaching agents to design pages that do not look machine-made.

executive_summary.headline: Key takeaway
executive_summary.body: The best builds this week package a craft, a phone or a whole studio as something an agent can drive and check by eye. Pick one task you do by hand and try a skill that renders and judges its own output.

top_picks.title: patch-gg/pixelfx
top_picks.summary: pixelfx is a free library of 244 pixel-art effects, each a small piece of code, plus a Claude Code skill that drafts, renders, looks and refines new ones. It was created Oct 30 and has 2,597 stars.
top_picks.results: 2,597 stars in its first two days (created Oct 30); 244 effects across fire, weather, UI, pickups and 12 chained attack moves; live gallery; MIT; 8 commits in the window.
key_takeaways: Effects drop into a browser game, or export as sprite sheets for any engine.
The skill works as a loop: draft, render, look at the frames, refine.
The method credits Hugo Duprez's write-up on making pixel-art effects with Claude.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is treating art as code the agent can render and judge by eye, so craft knowledge ships as a reusable skill. Experiment: write a skill for your own house style, such as slide diagrams or product renders, and let an agent produce ten variations in an afternoon.

top_picks.title: wangzan101/Mika
top_picks.summary: Mika is an on-device Android agent that takes a sentence, then works your apps and the web on a hidden background screen while you keep using the phone. It was created Oct 29 and has 3,860 stars.
top_picks.results: 3,860 stars in its first three days (created Oct 29); v0.1.33 on Nov 1; 100+ commits in the window; Apache-2.0; README demos include price-capped shopping, flight lookups and job-site outreach.
key_takeaways: Runs on a separate background screen, so the phone stays usable.
Demos: summarize a group chat, add the cheapest charger over 4.5 stars to the cart, read a creator's recent posts.
Works with any app or site; several demos use apps popular in China.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is the hidden second screen, which makes a phone agent something you can run all day without losing the device. Experiment: hand it one recurring errand, such as comparing prices or checking a feed, and time it against doing it yourself.

top_picks.title: haydenschmitty/floorplan
top_picks.summary: Floorplan has Claude or Codex read a codebase and draw an interactive, plain-English map of every part, file and web request. It was created Oct 27 and has 1,790 stars and a live demo.
top_picks.results: 1,790 stars in its first six days (created Oct 27); v0.6.1 on Nov 1; about 90 commits in the window; MIT; live demo map of a four-repo coffee-subscription app.
key_takeaways: Every part and connection gets a plain-English name, so non-coders can follow the app.
The map updates as the agent changes code, showing which parts a change touched.
Works with Claude Code and Codex.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is giving people who built an app with AI a map of it they can actually read. Experiment: run it on the messiest internal tool your team owns and ask a new teammate to explain checkout, or any core flow, using only the map.

top_picks.title: dbreunig/nesformer
top_picks.summary: nesformer compiles an NES CPU into the weights of a stock Qwen3.5 model, so Super Mario Bros. runs as the model predicts a CPU execution log one token at a time. The Show HN drew 292 points and 150 comments.
top_picks.results: 292 HN points and 150 comments (Oct 30); repo created Oct 30 with 263 stars; nobody trained the weights, a compiler computed every one; builds on Qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal.
key_takeaways: The model's Gated DeltaNet state acts as the machine's memory.
A small host program draws the picture and reads the controller; the model does the CPU.
Plays Super Mario Bros. World 1-1 and a homebrew game.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is showing that a language model's weights can be a program, which reframes what 'running a model' means. Experiment: have your scientists compile a small deterministic calculator or unit-converter into a model and compare its outputs token by token with plain code.

top_picks.title: patch-gg/anymove
top_picks.summary: anymove turns one AI-generated video of a creature into a rigged 3D animation: two camera views in one frame pin every joint, and the rig is fitted frame by frame and exported as a GLB. The maker puts a usable move at about $3 all in.
top_picks.results: Maker states about $3 for a usable move (README); 460 stars in its first days (created Oct 27); examples shown for dragon, giant spider, fire demon and wolf; Apache-2.0; 10 commits in the window.
key_takeaways: Works for wings, tails and eight legs, not just humanoids.
A joint reader trained on one creature finds joints in both views, and matching heights pin them in 3D.
Nine ready creatures, including T-rex, centaur and mech, are listed with 4 to 7 moves each.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is using a video model as a cheap motion-capture studio. Experiment: film a product or mechanism with a video model from two angles and see if the same trick yields a usable 3D motion path for a demo.

top_picks.title: muaaz9329/cheap-ag
top_picks.summary: cheap-ag splits coding work so Opus plans and a model costing about half a cent per task writes the code, with a test required before anything returns. The builder reports 63% fewer Opus tokens for the same feature and prompt.
top_picks.results: Builder reports 63% fewer Opus tokens for the same feature and prompt (README); 196 stars in its first four days (created Oct 28); v1.2.7 on Oct 31; 56 commits in the window; MIT.
key_takeaways: The cheap model works in its own copy of the project and must pass a test to hand work back.
Aimed at stretching a $20 or $100 Claude plan with a few dollars of DeepSeek.
Planner and typist roles mirror a senior engineer and a fast junior.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is paying the expensive model only to think, and gating the cheap model with tests. Experiment: run one week of your own side-project coding through this split and compare plan usage with the previous week.

top_picks.title: sitor-ai/frametell
top_picks.summary: Frametell turns a sentence, notes or PDFs into an explainer video: a director agent drafts a storyboard for sign-off, then narration, voice and animated pages. It is local-first and works with any model, and v0.7.4 shipped Oct 29.
top_picks.results: 453 stars (created Oct 10); v0.7.4 on Oct 29; 57 commits in the window; AGPL-3.0; README example is a 72-second film made in one desktop run.
key_takeaways: One sentence such as 'explain the uncertainty principle' is enough to start.
The storyboard is approved before narration and voice are produced.
Built for people who explain science, history, technology and books.
top_picks.enterprise_adaptation: The clever part is the storyboard checkpoint, which keeps a human in the creative seat while the agent does the production. Experiment: turn one dense research memo into a 60-second explainer and use it to open your next internal science review.
